Waren Wright
Preserved Primary Document • wright-n.htm
We know very little about the earliest WRIGHT ancestor within the mixed blood community. It is known from the
Lewes Cool Springs Presbyterian Church records that on November 21,
1799
, Nicholas Wright and Mary, "free mulattos", were married. Based on this, Nicholas was probably born sometime before
1780
.
Nicholas appears in the
1800
DE census records living in Dagsborough Hundred, Sussex Co. as the head of a household with 3 other "free colored" people. By
1810
the census shows him in a household of 6. Also appearing in the
1810
census records were
Daniel Wright and  Sarah Wright  but I do not know the connection between these three families.
There were also mixed race Wrights living in Kent County, DE and in nearby Maryland who may have been related to Nicholas.
The
1800
Kent County DE census shows:
George Wright as head of a Little Creek Hundred household of 6 "other free"
Ham Wright as head of a Little Creek Hundred household of 4 "other free"
Philip Wright as head of a Little Creek Hundred household of 5 "other free"
Nothing more is known about these two so far, but, based on information supplied by Stacey Emeharole, it possible that Nicholas and Mary had the following children:
Warren Wright  (b.c.
1803
) married Maria Sockum
